contentHtml:
THE NETHERLANDS—Royal Philips will propose three new Supervisory Board appointments at its 2027 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (AGM) to strengthen its business, financial, and medical technology expertise.

The health technology company has nominated Dick Boer, Laurence Debroux, and Todd J. Brinton to join the board, bringing experience in corporate leadership, financial management, governance and medical device innovation.

New board nominees bring business and medtech experience

Dick Boer, a former president and CEO of Ahold and Ahold Delhaize, will be proposed for appointment as vice-chairman of Philips’ Supervisory Board.

He led Ahold and subsequently Ahold Delhaize until 2018. From 2022 to 2025, he chaired the Supervisory Board of Just Eat Takeaway.

He currently serves as Deputy Chair and Senior Independent Director of Shell plc, as well as Lead Independent Director and Vice Chair of Nestlé S.A.

If shareholders approve his appointment, Boer will succeed Paul Stoffels as vice-chairman.

Laurence Debroux, a former Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Heineken, will be nominated to succeed Liz Doherty as Chair of Philips’ Audit Committee.

She served on Heineken’s Executive Board from 2015 to 2021 and previously held CFO positions at JCDecaux and Sanofi.

She currently serves on the boards of Randstad, where she chairs the Audit Committee, and Coca-Cola Europacific Partners.

She also served as an independent director of Exor until May 2026.

Todd J. Brinton, a physician and medical technology executive, will bring clinical and product innovation experience to the board.

He currently serves as Chief Scientific Officer and Corporate Vice President for Advanced Innovation and Technology at Edwards Lifesciences.

Previously, he was a clinical professor of medicine and adjunct professor of Bioengineering at Stanford University, where he also practised as an interventional cardiologist.

Brinton has founded several cardiovascular device companies, including Shockwave Medical, where he served as Chief Medical Officer.

Board changes and succession planning

The proposed appointments will accompany three departures at the close of the 2027 AGM.

Stoffels, who serves as vice-chairman and chair of the Quality and Regulatory Committee, will retire after nine years on the board.

Doherty will also step down when her current term expires, while Sanjay Poonen will leave ahead of the end of his second term to focus on other board responsibilities.

Meanwhile, John DeFord will succeed Stoffels as Chair of the Quality and Regulatory Committee, maintaining oversight of product quality and regulatory matters.

Commenting on the nominations, Feike Sijbesma, Chairman of Philips’ Supervisory Board, said the three candidates would strengthen the board’s international business, financial, governance and medical technology capabilities.

He also recognised the contributions of Stoffels, Doherty and Poonen during their tenure.

The proposed changes reflect Philips’ focus on board succession and oversight as the medical technology industry navigates product innovation, regulatory requirements and growing demands for financial and operational accountability.

The company will publish the 2027 AGM agenda and explanatory notes, including the proposed appointments, in due course in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
